purpose: Model-independent analog retrieval guidance. This is a conservative search ontology, not an electrically verified classifier or design textbook.

policy.containment: An op-amp containing a mirror remains an op-amp candidate. Put explicitly required subcircuits in required_blocks; keep parent-function evidence in hypotheses. A block may appear in many unrelated circuit families.
policy.hard_vs_soft: Literal counts and explicitly required supported wiring are hard. Wiring inferred from a family name is a hypothesis, never a compulsory universal definition.
policy.counts: more than=gt; at least=ge; fewer than=lt; at most=le; exactly=eq; no=eq 0; between inclusive endpoints=ge plus le. Total transistors includes nmos/pmos/npn/pnp. A transistor acting as a current source is NOT an independent current_source device.
policy.counts_guard: Application independently parses common count phrases. Use numerals with canonical physical nouns. Unrecognized counts require clarification rather than a guessed hard constraint. Do not equate 2 output ports with 2 total ports.
policy.terminal_contract: Device terminals are typed and ordered. All query entities must belong to one parent Circuit. Device aliases are distinct devices. Repeated net aliases mean equality; separate net aliases are always different physical nets. Reuse one alias for shared supplies; do not invent a separate output-stage source if its connection was not requested. Count-only passives do not need invented placement inside a connected signal-path pattern.
policy.device_roles: Input, output, tail, load, bias, reset and compensation are functional hypotheses unless independently grounded. Names such as CLK/VOUT are hints, not verified roles or waveforms. Explicit external clock requests require external plus clock_named on their gate/base control (VCLK/CLK/CLOCK/PHI/CK prefixes); an arbitrary VB bias is not equivalent. Supply/ground/rail conditions use recognized net-name conventions; external input/output signals additionally require not_rail. Bare gate/drain/source continuations for one transistor must refer to that same device.
policy.stage_count: Transistor stacks, signal nodes, buffers and capacitors do not independently establish stage count. Do not translate 3-stage op-amp into 3 cascodes or 3 capacitors. Numbered-stage candidate searches need disjoint, ordered signal-stage groups. A reciprocal gate-drain/base-collector regenerative branch is not an extra feedforward stage. Operating stage count still needs reviewed signal-path evidence or simulation.
policy.specs: Gain, GBW, delay, offset, kickback, noise, power, temperature coefficient, startup, stability, output swing, current ratio and supply range need values/models/test conditions or measured annotations. Mark them unverified, not new DB properties.
policy.text: Paper citations describe a source, not necessarily this exact subfigure. Numeric page references and auto-generated device counts are not functional descriptions.
policy.false_positive_policy: Explain both supporting wiring and competing explanations. Never say MATCH success or a high cosine confirms a function. Rank focused matches before incidental subblocks only when the user is searching for that block itself.
policy.prototype_mode: Generate 4–5 actual temporary netlists, not Cypher strings or numeric vectors. The parser and same graph encoder validate them. Variants must be distinct; no padding with disconnected devices. Never ingest or certify prototypes.
policy.unknown_terms: This list is not exhaustive. Preserve unknown family/topology wording, propose small supported physical hypotheses only if defensible, and list unresolved evidence. Do not force an unknown request into a listed class.
policy.rules_status: Curated search heuristics; graph patterns are schema-validated, not proven complete/necessary family definitions. Needs analog-engineer review and benchmark growth. Identical validated plans use identical compilation/ranking across providers. Different generated interpretations/prototypes may still yield different results.

device_contracts.roles: signal input, gain device, mirror, tail, cascode, switch, reset
device_contracts.limits: Polarity and wiring known; enhancement/depletion, Vth, gm, region and sizes not inferred.

device_contracts.roles: same physical roles as NMOS with opposite polarity; common pull-up/load devices
device_contracts.limits: Do not assume every PMOS is a load or every source is VDD.

device_contracts.roles: gain, differential input, mirror, junction reference
device_contracts.limits: Beta, emitter area, operating current and temperature behavior need actual model/value evidence.
Same caveats as NPN; do not invent collector/base ties.

device_contracts.roles: load, degeneration, feedback, bias, RC network
device_contracts.limits: Pin orientation has no physical polarity. Resistance values may be absent.

device_contracts.roles: load, storage, AC coupling, compensation, filtering, tank
device_contracts.limits: Presence alone proves none of these roles; capacitance and operating frequency may be absent.
Presence alone does not prove oscillation; inductance/Q/parasitics need evidence.
Canonical diode terminal names are p/n. A diode-connected transistor is still a transistor, not a diode device.

device_contracts.roles: explicit independent DC stimulus/supply in supported flat uploads
device_contracts.limits: VDD net is not automatically a voltage_source instance. Clock waveform support is not provided by the flat upload parser.

device_contracts.roles: explicit independent DC source in supported uploads
device_contracts.limits: Do not count a MOS bias transistor as this physical type.
One macro is one device, not two hidden MOS transistors; do not infer internal layout.
Native macro has one declared control terminal; do not invent a second complementary control.
No inferred transistor implementation or timing.
Macro membership is exact; PLL lock/phase noise are not verified.

unsupported_device_classes.handling: Not native canonical types. Do not substitute MOS/BJT without a verified upstream conversion.
Technology/model subtypes are not independently preserved by generic nmos/pmos labels.
Dedicated models not supported by this upload parser. A capacitor is not proof of a varactor; an LC network is not proof of a crystal.
Do not invent canonical physical types or expand opaque blocks. Future parser adapters are needed.

primitives.name: Input pair plus regenerative load candidate
primitives.description: A distinct-gate input pair directly drives a complementary cross-coupled load; stronger comparator candidate evidence than a lone pair.
look_for: opposite-polarity cross-coupled load on the pair drains
limits: This represents one comparator subset, not all comparators. Clock/reset and decision behavior remain unverified.

primitives.name: MOS current mirror
primitives.description: Same-polarity MOS pair with one gate-drain-tied reference and a second distinct drain; shared gate/source.
false_positives: bias/load mirror inside amplifier, oscillator, regulator or comparator
limits: current copying/ratio/compliance requires operating-point and size evidence

primitives.name: MOS differential pair
primitives.description: Same-polarity MOS pair with shared source, distinct gates and distinct drains; gates are separate from their drain/tail nets.
look_for: loads or tail device as contextual evidence
false_positives: common-source devices merely sharing a supply
limits: No input port labels or valid tail current are assumed.

primitives.name: BJT current mirror
primitives.description: Same-polarity BJT pair sharing bases/emitters; reference collector=base and output collector distinct.
limits: Beta/base-current error and current ratio unknown.

primitives.name: MOS cascode candidate
primitives.description: A drain-to-source stack with separate control gates; a partial branch, not a stage count.
limits: Need gate bias and signal-path context to establish cascode operation.

primitives.name: Cross-coupled regenerative pair
primitives.description: Each MOS gate connects to the other device's drain; opposite output nodes must differ.
limits: No clock/reset or differential comparison is proved by this motif alone.

primitives.name: Complementary inverter-shaped pair
primitives.description: NMOS/PMOS share gate and drain with separate source nets.
limits: Rail identities, logic levels and switching behavior remain unverified.

primitives.name: Series RC branch
primitives.description: Resistor and capacitor share one intermediate net; exposed endpoints differ.
look_for: R and C connected in a path
limits: No cutoff, zero, filter family or compensation function without context/values.

primitives.name: Clock-controlled tail candidate
primitives.description: A switch drain connects to an input-pair common source; its gate is a candidate clock/control net.
limits: Net names cannot prove periodic clock or evaluate/reset phases.

primitives.name: Reset/precharge network candidate
primitives.description: Controlled MOS paths connect candidate dynamic nodes to a common rail or equalize them.
limits: Need clock waveform and phase relationship for dynamic-operation proof.

primitives.name: Compensation-capacitor candidate
primitives.description: Capacitor spans candidate signal-stage nodes, sometimes through a series nulling resistor.
look_for: cap between internal gain node and later signal output
limits: Stability, pole splitting and stage count require signal-path identification and AC analysis.

primitives.name: BJT differential pair candidate
primitives.description: Same-polarity BJTs with shared emitter, separate bases and collector branches.
false_positives: bias network sharing an emitter rail
limits: Input function and operating currents unknown.

primitives.name: Source/emitter follower candidate
primitives.description: Input controls gate/base; output is source/emitter with an appropriate bias/load branch.
limits: Voltage gain and buffering ability require operating conditions.

primitives.name: Common-source/emitter gain candidate
primitives.description: Input at gate/base, output at drain/collector; source/emitter bias provides reference/degeneration.
limits: No linear gain or inversion proven without bias evidence.

primitives.name: LC resonant-network candidate
primitives.description: Connected inductors/capacitors in a candidate resonance path.

primitives.name: Diode-connected transistor
primitives.description: MOS gate=drain or BJT base=collector. Device retains its transistor type.
false_positives: bias/reference/load junction with unrelated overall function
limits: Voltage/current relationship needs a device model.

primitives.name: Resistive feedback/divider candidate
primitives.description: Two resistor branches meet at a sense node; feedback requires a known controlled signal path.
limits: Gain, reference voltage and loop stability unknown.

families.description: Differential high-gain amplifier intended for feedback operation.
look_for: input pair, bias, active loads and signal gain path

families.description: Differential input produces output-current behavior.
Amplifies a difference between two signals.
look_for: distinct signal inputs and shared tail plus loads

families.description: Candidate cascaded gain path with interstage compensation.
look_for: input stage drives a separate gain device

families.description: Candidate differential gain core with stacked input/cascode and load branches.
Candidate input signal currents routed into opposite-polarity folded branches.
look_for: input drains connect into complementary folding branches
not_required: two stages or a Miller capacitor
cannot_verify: folding without complete signal-path context, gain/swing

families.description: Auxiliary amplifier controls a cascode/bias node.
look_for: local sensing path returns to cascode gate

families.description: Candidate differential decision circuit; output is intended to indicate input ordering.
look_for: input comparison path plus decision/output context
not_required: clock, latch, capacitor or particular transistor count

families.description: Clock phases control input evaluation and reset/regeneration.
look_for: comparison pair, control-gated tail/path and reset plus regenerative output
not_required: a capacitor device; parasitics may supply dynamic capacitance

families.description: A known dynamic comparator family combining differential evaluation and regenerative latch behavior.
look_for: combined input/tail and regenerative output topology
not_required: one exact transistor count across variants
cannot_verify: family subtype without full connection review

families.description: Candidate dynamic comparator separates input evaluation and latch-tail sections.
look_for: distinct controlled input and latch current paths
not_required: merely any two NMOS at ground
false_positives: bias branches or duplicate tails in an amplifier
cannot_verify: phase and family proof from tail count alone

families.description: Decision thresholds depend on output state through positive feedback.
look_for: decision output fed back to comparison path

families.description: A standalone current-copying network or embedded bias/load block, depending on request scope.
not_required: entire parent circuit must be a mirror when the user asks 'contains a mirror'

families.description: Bias network intended to establish current without an external precision current.
look_for: bias loop, resistive/device reference branch and possible startup

families.description: Reference candidate combines temperature-dependent junction terms and scaled differences.
look_for: multiple junction branches and resistive/amplifier feedback context
false_positives: BJT amplifier or generic bias reference
cannot_verify: area/current-density ratios, temperature compensation, reference voltage

families.description: Circuit intended to establish a stable reference voltage.
Feedback controls a pass device to regulate an output.
look_for: pass path, sensed output and error-control loop

families.description: Frequency-selective circuit; passive and active realizations differ.
look_for: R/C/L or OTA-C signal network and input-output path
cannot_verify: filter response/order/cutoff without values and transfer analysis

families.description: Candidate signal path accumulates input charge/current on capacitive state.
look_for: feedback or transconductance current into a capacitor

families.description: Switch phases route capacitors between signal/reference nodes.
look_for: capacitor storage and control-gated switch paths
not_required: assume a control name is a clock

families.description: Switch samples a signal onto storage, optionally buffered.
Active circuit sustains oscillation with an LC frequency-selective network.
look_for: tank plus appropriate active feedback/negative-resistance path
not_required: cross coupling alone proves comparator or oscillator

families.description: Loop of inverting delay stages can sustain oscillation.
not_required: three transistor stacks mean three stages

families.description: Threshold switching and charge/discharge state form an oscillation cycle.
look_for: storage node, charging paths and threshold feedback

families.description: Switched current/charge paths drive an output/storage node.
look_for: controlled sourcing/sinking branches or switched capacitor network

families.description: Feedback system combines phase detection, filtering and controlled oscillation.
look_for: PFD/phase detector context, control filter, VCO and feedback
not_required: PFD macro alone proves an entire PLL

families.description: Time-varying/nonlinear switching combines signal and local-oscillator paths.
not_required: ordinary differential pair is a mixer

families.description: Amplifier intended for low-noise input signal amplification.
Current-input to voltage-output amplifier, typically with feedback.
look_for: input summing/sense node and feedback to output
not_required: every feedback resistor is a TIA

families.description: Output common-mode sensing adjusts a bias/control node.
look_for: two output sense paths and shared control return
